LESSON: FAMILY NEEDS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Social Environment
Topic 1.3: Family Needs
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 13

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Family Needs, part of Social Environment in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we choose foods to take in our family? 2. How do you choose the food you eat?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Family Needs together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: Interacting with digital devices as learners record poems and songs on different family needs.

• Self-Efficacy: Courage as the learner sorts and groups assorted locally available food items into types of tastes.

13

Values:
• Respect: Patience is enhanced as learners appreciate diverse opinions while sharing information on different family needs.

• Responsibility: Self-initiative is nurtured as learners make a nature corner with different food items found in the locality.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life skills Issues: Self-awareness as learners draw, colour and group family needs.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Religious Education Activities: Physical needs of the family as learners share information on different family needs.
